statement: The function returns a result r, and r is exactly the number of pairs (i, j) of integers with 0 <= i < j < n for which nums1[i] - nums1[j] <= nums2[i] - nums2[j] + diff. All arithmetic in this inequality is exact integer arithmetic; under the preconditions every term involved is small enough that no overflow can occur.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). The constraints hold: len(nums1) = len(nums2) = n, 2 <= n <= 100000, for every k with 0 <= k < n both -10000 <= nums1[k] <= 10000 and -10000 <= nums2[k] <= 10000, and -10000 <= diff <= 10000.

preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). The constraints hold: len(nums1) = len(nums2) = n, n = 2, for every k with 0 <= k < 2 both -10000 <= nums1[k] <= 10000 and -10000 <= nums2[k] <= 10000, and -10000 <= diff <= 10000.

statement: For 0 <= i < j < n define d(i,j) = (nums1[i] - nums2[i]) - (nums1[j] - nums2[j]), and let m = min { d(i,j) : 0 <= i < j < n }, which is well-defined because n >= 2. The function returns a result r, and r = 0 if and only if diff < m.

statement: For 0 <= i < j < n define d(i,j) = (nums1[i] - nums2[i]) - (nums1[j] - nums2[j]), and let M = max { d(i,j) : 0 <= i < j < n }, which is well-defined because n >= 2. The function returns a result r, and r = n*(n-1)/2 if and only if diff >= M.
